title: Preventive Maintenance Agreements — Ruling on One Live Agreement per Site
content:
## Contract administration ruling

**Ruling.** A building owner may hold any number of Preventive Maintenance Agreements at once, but never more than one agreement in proposed, active, pending renewal or suspended status for the same site. A proposal for a site that already carries an agreement in one of those statuses is not issued as a second agreement; the existing agreement is amended instead through a schedule change. Agreements in expired, cancelled, declined or withdrawn status do not block a new proposal for the same site, so a building owner whose previous agreement lapsed is proposed a fresh one. Each agreement is priced, billed and renewed on its own record, and no entitlement, allowance or balance is ever shared between two agreements of the same owner.

**No ceiling on the portfolio.** The company sets no maximum number of agreements per building owner; the only limit is the one-per-site rule above.

### What decides whether a second proposal may issue

The decisive fact is the status of any agreement already on record for the same site, read from the agreement records, not from what the caller says about the site. The proposal is tested against the site, so an agreement at another building of the same owner has no bearing.

| Status of the agreement already on record for the site | A new proposal for that site |
|---|---|
| proposed | not issued; the existing record is amended through a schedule change |
| active | not issued; the existing record is amended through a schedule change |
| pending renewal | not issued; the existing record is amended through a schedule change |
| suspended | not issued; the existing record is amended through a schedule change |
| expired | may issue as a fresh agreement |
| cancelled | may issue as a fresh agreement |
| declined | may issue as a fresh agreement |
| withdrawn | may issue as a fresh agreement |

### Illustrations (hypothetical)

- An owner holds an active agreement at one building and a suspended agreement at a second building, and asks for a proposal at a third building: the third building carries no agreement, so a proposal for it may issue, and the count of the owner's agreements does not matter.
- An owner whose agreement at a building expired last season asks for a new one there: an expired agreement does not block a proposal, so a fresh agreement is proposed for that site.
- An owner asks to add two rooftop units at a building that already holds an active agreement: no second agreement is issued; the existing agreement's schedule is changed instead.
